title: Withhold dependent claims until the prerequisite has delivery evidence
description:
Objective: stop dependent work building on a promise the recorded delivery does not support. Today dependsOn gating keys purely on the prerequisite's status reaching DONE or ARCHIVED, so a task that reached DONE without a landed commit still releases everything waiting on it.

Deliverable: the dependency satisfaction check in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/dependencyUnblock.ts and the claim gating in tools/claimNextTask.ts additionally require that a DONE prerequisite satisfies the project's delivery policy. A prerequisite that is DONE but lacks the required evidence keeps its dependents withheld, and the claim result explains exactly which prerequisite and which evidence is missing.

Not in scope: changing what dependsOn means for planning, which still proceeds, or the auto-unblock of blockedOnTaskIds targets beyond applying the same evidence rule. Under the default behaviour-preserving delivery policy nothing changes, so existing projects see no difference.

Unskips the acceptance case "a failed required gate cannot release dependents".

Verification: npx vitest run src/state/dependencyUnblock.test.ts src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts from packages/moe-daemon.
definitionOfDone: A DONE prerequisite lacking the evidence its delivery policy requires keeps its dependents unclaimable
The refusal names the prerequisite task and the specific missing evidence
Planning on a dependent task still proceeds, matching the existing rule that dependsOn gates WORKING-status claims only
The blockedOnTaskIds auto-unblock applies the same evidence rule rather than releasing on status alone
Under the default delivery policy behaviour is unchanged and the existing dependency tests stay green unmodified
The acceptance case for a failed required gate not releasing dependents is unskipped and passes unchanged
npx vitest run src/state/dependencyUnblock.test.ts src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts passes and npm test in packages/moe-daemon stays green
taskRails: dependsOn still gates WORKING-status claims only; planning must keep proceeding.
Missing or deleted prerequisite ids keep counting as satisfied, as they do today.

implementationPlan.description: READ THE HELD-OUT CASE AS THE CONTRACT AND MAP THE ONE SHARED SEAM (read-only, no edits). Extract the exact contract. The strict policy is `deliveryPolicy: 'local-branch'` with `qualityGate: 'node gate.cjs'` and `qualityGateScope: 'everyTask'`, so the required gate command comes from the existing qualityGate setting and the policy switch is deliveryPolicy; an absent or default policy must change nothing. Enumerate every caller of that function before changing it and confirm the cycle-detection helpers use `dependencyEdges` instead, because the evidence rule must never reach cycle detection. Read whatever they landed and use it verbatim. Produce no diff in this step.

implementationPlan.description: PUT THE EVIDENCE RULE IN THE ONE SHARED PLACE. In src/state/dependencyUnblock.ts add a function that reports a prerequisite's shortfall rather than a bare boolean: it returns whether the prerequisite satisfies its dependents and, when it does not, the list of missing evidence as prefixed strings. Then make the existing `isDependencySatisfied` delegate to it and keep returning a boolean, so `unmetDependsOn`, `unmetBlockedOnTaskIds` and every current caller inherit the new rule with no signature change and the auto-unblock path needs no separate edit. Order the checks so today's behaviour is untouched wherever the policy does not demand evidence: a prerequisite that is missing from the board counts satisfied exactly as it does now, a prerequisite whose status is not DONE or ARCHIVED is unmet for the existing reason with no evidence claim attached, and only a DONE prerequisite under a policy that requires a gate is asked for evidence. Resolve the policy and the required command through the helper delivered by task-c484696db72c4ce4855dfc599a7b2072 and do NOT re-implement the matching rules locally: the four decoy records exist precisely to catch a second, subtly different implementation. If that helper turns out to be shaped only as a can-this-task-go-DONE check rather than a reusable predicate over any task, EXTRACT the predicate into something both callers share rather than copying it, and say so in the step note. Error handling: a store read that fails, or evidence records that cannot be resolved, must report the evidence as MISSING and withhold, never fall through to satisfied — failing open here would release a dependent on exactly the promise this card exists to check. Add no new record type and no migration.

planningNotes.risks: The defect that would pass review is a lookup that is close but not exact — keyed on the task instead of its current candidate, on the candidate id without its tree, on any command, or on any source. Each has its own unit case for exactly that reason, so a regression names which lookup broke instead of failing as one opaque acceptance timeout. Second, this change sits under a function with many callers: the evidence rule must not reach cycle detection, and the existing dependency tests must pass UNMODIFIED, so any need to edit them is evidence that default behaviour moved. Third, the refusal must be thrown here even though the finalizing hold earlier in this epic is returned — the two acceptance cases genuinely differ and generalising from the other one produces a resolved call the capture helper rejects. Fourth, both prerequisites are unlanded, so the consumed helper may arrive in a different shape than assumed; extract rather than copy, and report it. Finally, state the boundary honestly in the completion: this card withholds on RECORDED evidence and re-runs nothing, so a check record that lies about a gate it never ran still releases a dependent — binding that record to an observed run is the runner and receipt work, not this card.
